Cytochalasin B is known to inhibit actin polymerization by binding to the barbed end of actin filaments, which are microfilaments.  
Microspikes of the growth cone contain actin filaments (microfilaments), not microtubules.  
Cytochalasin B causes depolymerization of these microfilaments, but this effect is reversible upon removal of the drug.  
Thus, the correct description is that microfilaments in the microspike undergo reversible depolymerization.
